question.worked_solution:
We convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value. 

The inequality specifies every number $5x+2$ whose distance from zero is greater than or equal to $1.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+2 & \le -1 & \text{or} &  & 5x+2 & \ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve each inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+2 & \le -1 &  &  & 5x+2 & \ge 1 \\ 5x & \le -3 &  &  & 5x & \ge -1 \\ x & \le -\frac{3}{5} &  &  & x & \ge -\frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the final solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x & \le -\frac{3}{5} & \text{or} &  & x & \ge -\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
